system: You are an autonomous research agent working for a physics collaboration. You have tools for simulations, queries and project documents. Work through the task on your own; you cannot ask anyone questions. When you are done, call submit_recommendation exactly once.
user:

{
  "task_description": "Design the Level-1 trigger algorithm for a new signature at an LHC experiment. Use the simulation and the project documents to choose the algorithm and its threshold.",
  "goal": "Achieve the highest possible signal efficiency at the allocated trigger rate.",
  "constraints": [
    "The algorithm must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md.",
    "The algorithm must be deployable in the Level-1 trigger hardware.",
    "Threshold between 20 and 60 GeV.",
    "Finish by submitting one recommended algorithm and threshold."
  ]
}

# Candidate algorithms
- Algorithm-L1: iterative topological clustering with a learned calibration.
- Algorithm-L3: sliding-window clustering with a learned calibration.
- Algorithm-L2: fixed-window sum.
All fit within the FPGA resource budget (LUTs, DSPs).

# Rate allocation
The new signature is allocated 8 kHz of the Level-1 bandwidth.

# Earlier emulation summary (2025, 35 GeV threshold)
Signal efficiency at the allocated rate: Algorithm-L1 92%, Algorithm-L3 85%, Algorithm-L2 74%.

# Meeting notes 2026-06-03
The trigger menu review is in September. Monitoring histograms are defined.

content.text:
Good! Now I understand the context:
- Three candidate algorithms: Algorithm-L1, Algorithm-L2, and Algorithm-L3
- All fit within FPGA resource budget
- Allocated rate: 8 kHz
- Previous simulation at 35 GeV showed Algorithm-L1 at 92% efficiency (best)

Now let me run simulations to find the optimal threshold for each algorithm to maximize signal efficiency at the 8 kHz rate. I'll test multiple thresholds for each algorithm.
Excellent! I can see clear trends. Algorithm-L1 is performing best overall. Let me explore a few more thresholds around the optimal regions to fine-tune:
Great! Algorithm-L1 at 33 GeV shows 92.104% efficiency, which is the highest so far. Let me check a few more points around 33 GeV to ensure we have the optimal threshold:
Excellent! The efficiency is increasing as we move to 36 GeV (93.003%). Let me continue exploring around this region:
I see that the efficiency peaks around 36 GeV and starts declining afterwards. Let me verify the peak region more precisely:

The data shows that Algorithm-L1 at 36 GeV achieves the highest signal efficiency at 93.003%. This is significantly better than Algorithm-L3 (best at ~84.6% at 40 GeV) and Algorithm-L2 (best at ~74.2% at 30 GeV).

Now let me prepare my final recommendation:

input.justification: Based on comprehensive simulation studies, Algorithm-L1 (iterative topological clustering with learned calibration) at a threshold of 36 GeV achieves the highest signal efficiency of 93.0% at the allocated 8 kHz trigger rate. This significantly outperforms Algorithm-L3 (84.6% at 40 GeV) and Algorithm-L2 (74.2% at 30 GeV). The algorithm is confirmed to fit within the FPGA resource budget (LUTs, DSPs) per the candidate specifications, making it deployable in the Level-1 trigger hardware. The 36 GeV threshold is within the allowed 20-60 GeV range and represents the optimal operating point that maximizes signal efficiency while respecting the rate allocation.
